newsitem.title: USA: Waigel - Germany to cut deficit to 2.9 pct this yr.
newsitem.headline: Waigel - Germany to cut deficit to 2.9 pct this yr.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel said on Tuesday that Germany would succeed in paring back its budget deficit in 1997 and meet the strict entry criteria for Europe's currency union.

"Yes we stick by our goal of bringing the budget deficit down to 2.9 percent. Of course, the target (the budget deficit goal for EMU) is three percent," Waigel told reporters after delivering a speech at the German American Chamber of Commerce Inc.
Waigel also expected monetary union would begin as scheduled on January 1, 1999.
"I expect EMU will take place on time," Waigel said.

In order to join the currency union, Europeoan Union member nations must meet a number of strict entry criteria, including presenting a budget deficit that is no higher than three percent of gross domestic product.
Talk about Germany's ability to meet this goal has become the hot topic of political debate as high unemployment and sluggish economic growth cast doubt Germany can meet the criteria.
Waigel said he is committed to paring back the budget deficit and he had even promised ex-Fed Chairman Paul Volcker that Germany's budget deficit would be reduced.
With Volcker at his side, Waigel said: "Paul Volcker made me write this down and if Germany misses this I could never come back to New York."
When asked about other nations' chances to join monetary union, Waigel declined to make any forecast.
"Every nation has its chance," Waigel said, adding that next March the 1997 economic data and projections for 1998 economic data would allow a decision to be made.
